chapter: Music scene, school and father's advice
title: Father's advice: play all types of music
summary: His father told him to learn all kinds of music in order to make a living, and Russell contrasts New Orleans bands with northern ones.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: If you're going to learn music, do it just like anything else. If you was a carpenter you couldn't tell me you couldn't build a two-story house. You couldn't build just one story. So if you're going to play music, try to play all type of music if you've got to make a living out. And I never will forget that. So that's why, I mean, I try to play all the music. I mean, I love the New Orleans music, but sometimes I can't make a living out. And that's all I can do is play the music.

I know down here though, the dancers, they always, that impressed me too when I first came down, they always played waltzes and other kinds of pieces. Up, say in New York, if you'd ask Eddie Conner or somebody to play a waltz, they'd be insulted. They'd say, get out of here, this is a jazz band. But down here they play all the guys. That's one thing you've got to give to the New Orleans musicians.
They try to satisfy, you know, the guests, you know.
Yeah, I've always noticed that too as being one of the main features of the bands here.
What type of music come up now, I try to get a little bit of it, learn a little bit of it, make it out. Your father actually impressed you with that.
That's one thing I never will forget. Very interesting, isn't it? Yeah. I mean, you know, they got some fellas, they'll cater to just one type of music.

Well, if you're cater to one type of music, it's all right if that's your sideline, but if you're going to make a living out of it, well, you've got to get with everything. Yeah, sure, that's right. Music is music with me. Yeah. But you've got something you like, you know.
